reasons.b: Fixed is a two-fold run split (select on run 0, evaluate on run 1, and reverse), the split-data remedy of KRI09; same map, cut-off, per-subject mean, mean>=0.30 and one-sided t.
reasons.c: The twins differ in exactly one line (the folds list), checked with diff; everything outside the criterion body equals the frozen skeleton.
reasons.d: Listed comparisons: the incomplete-beta convergence test (numerical), x.mean()>=0.30 (the claim's own threshold), len(x)<5 and sd>0 guards (allowed). Nothing inspects the input distribution.
reasons.e: No banned stem of PREREG section 4 occurs in the claim, data keys, meanings or sizes (substring scan of the whole brief); the brief gives a positive claim with its statistic and threshold and never says what 'claim false' means.
reasons.f: 20 subjects, 2 runs, 60 voxels: KRI09 gives no subject counts (its Example 2 simulates 30x30x20 voxels); voxels at the 60 cap. Sizes not documented by the source; reduced to the cap.
reasons.g: Same helpers, statistic, cut-off, threshold and test; the fixed does two cheap passes instead of one.

reasons.a: Faulty runs a one-way ANOVA across orientations on all 16 trials, takes the preferred orientation (argmax of the same means) and computes the selectivity index from the same means (sel_r, ev_r = r, r): selecting neurons by selectivity and then reporting their selectivity on the same data (KRI09 single-cell example).
reasons.b: Fixed selects tuned neurons and preferred orientation on even trials and computes the index on odd trials (standard split-trial remedy); same ANOVA, p<0.05, index and 0.25 threshold.
reasons.c: One line differs (sel_r, ev_r). The index clip and the den>0 guard are in both twins.
reasons.d: Listed: idx[tuned].mean()>=0.25 (claim threshold). Borderline note only: np.clip(idx,-1,1) was added after a pre-check of the fixed criterion on noise (LOG: index ratio exploding on N(0,1) data). It is not a branch, does not test the input, is a no-op for the non-negative rates of the brief, and is identical in both twins, so I answer yes; the designer may wish to disclose it.
reasons.e: No banned stem of PREREG section 4 occurs in the claim, data keys, meanings or sizes (substring scan of the whole brief); the brief gives a positive claim with its statistic and threshold and never says what 'claim false' means.
reasons.f: 150 neurons, 8 orientations, 16 trials: KRI09 states no counts for single-unit studies. Sizes not documented by the source; within the 300-unit cap.
reasons.g: Same ANOVA, index, guard and threshold; the halves change only the number of trials used.

reasons.b: Fixed splits on block 1, a separate early measurement whose noise is independent of block 0 in the skeleton (iid per-block noise), keeping the claim's own improvement definition; a standard independent-measure correction. reasons.a: Faulty restricts to patients with entry SBP>=150, then tests the mean 12-week lowering in the drug arm alone (one-sample t, mean>=5, one-sided), ignoring the placebo arm: change in a sub-sample selected on the noisy baseline value (BAR05 abstract, verified). The full text was not accessible and I did not obtain it.
reasons.b: Fixed compares the lowering between drug and placebo among patients with entry SBP>=150 (Welch, difference>=5, one-sided): a control arm selected the same way cancels regression to the mean; a standard remedy (control-group design).
reasons.c: The twins differ in one decision block (lines 107-114), but that block is the whole correction (the test changes from one-sample to two-sample because a control arm is added); no other line differs.
reasons.d: Listed: convergence test, a.var+b.var>0 (zero-variance guard) in the fixed, claim thresholds x.mean()>=5.0 and diff>=5.0 (claim constants). Nothing inspects the input distribution.

reasons.g: The statistic changes from a one-sample to a two-sample Welch t, which is inherent to adding the control arm; threshold 5, the one-sided p<0.05 rule and the cost are the same. Weakest pair for (c) and (g); accepted because the difference is the correction itself. Guard sizes differ (5 vs 3 per arm), both allowed.
